paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus turns the world's scoreboard upside down. The poor, the hungry and the weeping are called blessed, and Jesus says to them, "yours is the kingdom of God" (Luke 6:20). The rich, the well fed and the ones everybody praises get woes, because comfort that arrives early is not the prize (Luke 6:24-26). I spent years with nothing but dust, so I'm telling you, this news lands HARD.

Then Jesus asks for something bigger than being nice to nice people. He says, "Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you," and He points out that even sinners love those who love them (Luke 6:27, 32). Anybody can pay back kindness with kindness. Jesus wants love that doesn't wait for a reason, because the Most High "is kind to the ungrateful and wicked" (Luke 6:35). I think that's the whole heart of it: you're not copying the crowd, you're copying your Father.

So what does that mean for you, baker? "Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful" (Luke 6:36). That means a little less judging, a little more forgiving, and hands that stay open even when it costs you. And Jesus says the giving never goes to waste, because a good measure will be "running over" into your lap (Luke 6:38). That's one Jesus-sized cookie box, and the lid is NOT closing.
